historical_reviews.deepseek: Conflates this inventory row with the following write operation and supplies only tool version output.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Separates non-write firmware inventory from upgrade/downgrade and requires per-device comparison.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Row268 owns the actual NVFlash write; no ROM, force flag, reboot or version change belongs in this row.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Validates nvflash_mfg mode and cross-checks every GPU/NVSwitch identity so a tool banner cannot be mistaken for device firmware evidence.

original_test_intent: Use a validated non-write NVFlash manufacturing query from the host OS to inventory firmware for every GPU and NVSwitch and compare each physical device with the approved expected manifest.
original_method: Pin nvflash_mfg binary/hash and prove --v semantics; inventory GPU UUID/BDF and NVSwitch/topology first; preserve logs; execute only documented read-only queries; capture complete output/exit status, map every result to a device and cross-check with independent NVIDIA inventory; compare to manifest without flashing or rebooting.
manual_activity: Operator supplies approved tool and expected per-device manifest and confirms the non-write boundary; agent may run the validated inventory query and compare evidence.
required_inputs: Approved nvflash_mfg binary/hash for exact OS, architecture and devices
Documented proof that selected --v path is read-only
Protected evidence location and access approval
safety_requirements: Inspect help/provenance and reject any write, ROM, force or downgrade options
Never use credentialed SSH or bypass host identity from DeepSeek example
Preserve rather than clear dmesg/SEL baseline
Stop on unmapped device, unexpected prompt or write-capable behavior
A mismatch is evidence only and never permission to flash
agent_execution_scope: Validate binary/hash/read-only behavior and target map
Run approved version queries without state change
Cross-check output against independent inventory and manifest
engineer_actions: Approve tool, mapping and expected versions

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `nvflash --version` may report only utility version and DeepSeek incorrectly introduces images/reboot; it does not prove every device firmware.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-documented non-write `./nvflash_mfg --v` invocation or exact approved equivalent per mapped device, retain raw output and cross-check with nvidia-smi/NVSwitch inventory.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Literal nvflash_mfg --v and ten/thirty-minute estimates are preserved; no upgrade or reboot is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Produce a table joining device UUID/BDF/topology, independent inventory, nvflash firmware fields, expected value and comparison status while recording the binary hash and argv.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Distinguishes utility version from firmware values and proves completeness across GPUs and NVSwitches.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No actual upgrade/downgrade or post-flash recovery is claimed; that coverage remains solely in row268.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Vendor tooling is write-capable, so execution must be constrained to a reviewed non-write argument set.

project_override_considerations: Firmware owner defines canonical firmware fields and expected versions per GPU/NVSwitch SKU and approved tool release.
expected_evidence: nvflash_mfg binary origin/hash/version and reviewed help
Exact argv/exit status and complete raw output
Expected manifest revision and per-device comparison

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Although grouped under an upgrade/downgrade test set, the row's item, Procedure and Criteria consistently define a read-only version check; DeepSeek's flash expansion is not source authority.

blocked_analysis.analysis: An approved tool and manifest are provisionable project inputs; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Protects the read-only boundary and requires complete per-device firmware evidence rather than a utility banner.
independent_technical_reasoning: NVFlash family tools can expose both query and write paths, so binary provenance and exact argument review matter even when the intended action is read-only. A bare `--version` often describes the executable rather than every attached device; complete coverage requires mapping device-specific firmware fields to the platform topology and checking for omissions. Keeping writes in the next source row prevents accidental scope escalation.
